title: Your Say News - Overview
description: Whole-service health for post-service, the sole backend deployable. Use the domain dashboards for per-domain detail.

list.name: service
list.label: Service
list.description: post-service is the sole backend deployable.

panels.title: Error percentage
panels.description: Errors as a share of all instrumented work - API requests plus internal domain operations and background jobs. Expected rejections are not errors.

panels.title: Expected rejections
panels.description: Contract-defined refusals such as locked results. Tracked separately so they stay visible without inflating the error total.

panels.title: 5xx responses
panels.description: Every 5xx is an error. This panel exists on its own so a server fault is never hidden inside a combined error rate.

panels.title: Unexpected 4xx responses
panels.description: 4xx responses the endpoint contract does not define as normal. These count as errors.

panels.title: Expected rejections
panels.description: Refusals the contract defines as normal - kept visible but excluded from errors.

panels.title: Top 10 errors
panels.description: Grouped by stable error code and exception type - never by raw message or stack trace.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (domain, operation, error_type, error_code) (increase(yoursay_domain_errors_total{environment=~"$environment", domain=~"$domain"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Responses by status class
panels.description: Grouped by class rather than by individual code so the panel stays readable.

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, domain, operation) (rate(yoursay_domain_request_duration_milliseconds_bucket{environment=~"$environment", domain=~"$domain"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Traffic, errors and latency by domain
panels.description: Requests, errors and p95 latency side by side, so an unhealthy domain is obvious before opening its own dashboard.

panels.title: Internal operation rate by domain
panels.description: Domain work that has no public API of its own, such as feed ranking and Unwrapped research.

panels.title: Postgres pool connections
panels.description: post-service uses Hibernate Reactive, so the pool is the Vert.x SQL client pool rather than Agroal. Exhaustion looks like idle at zero with waiting climbing.

panels.title: Postgres pool wait and hold time
panels.description: Sustained wait time means the pool is too small or queries are too slow.

panels.title: Database statements per second
panels.description: Query volume. A jump here without a matching jump in requests means a new N+1.

panels.title: Transactions per second by result
panels.description: Rolled-back transactions are a failure signal even when the API returned 200.

panels.title: Connection acquisition and flushes per second
Worker pool saturation
panels.description: Blocking work runs here. A growing queue means requests are waiting for a worker.

panels.title: AI research provider outcomes
panels.description: The only outbound HTTP dependency with metrics today. Keycloak and S3 calls are not instrumented as metrics - see ADR-047.

panels.title: Background job runs per second
panels.description: A failed job is an error even though it never produces an HTTP 5xx.

panels.title: Garbage collection pause time
panels.description: Milliseconds of GC pause per second of wall clock. Sustained high values mean memory pressure, and show up as latency in every domain at once.

panels.title: Process uptime
panels.description: A reset to zero is a restart. Correlate with error spikes.

panels.title: Seconds since last JVM metric
panels.description: JVM metrics are emitted continuously regardless of traffic, so staleness here means the metrics pipeline itself is broken - not that the service is idle.

panels.title: Seconds since last domain metric
panels.description: Instrumentation freshness. Unlike the JVM panel this legitimately grows when nobody is using the app, so it is only a fault when read together with live traffic.

panels.title: Log lines received per second
panels.description: Logs reach Loki over OTLP. If this flatlines while metrics keep flowing, the logging pipeline is broken rather than the service being quiet.

panels.title: Domains reporting
panels.description: Expected over a busy range: autopost, feed, posts, postagent, topics, unwrapped, user, usercharacteristic, social, votes, platform. A drop means a route stopped being attributed to its domain, or an 'unknown' has appeared.

panels.title: Routes attributed to no domain
panels.description: A new controller whose path prefix is not in DomainRequestFilter lands here and is then missing from every domain dashboard. This should stay at zero.

panels.title: Telemetry export failures per second
panels.description: The collector dropping telemetry. Anything above zero means these dashboards are under-reporting, so read every other panel with suspicion.

panels.title: Failing traces
panels.description: Jump from a dashboard error to the request that produced it.
